title: Ignore uncovered lines?
body:
Not sure if this idea has any controversy nor has been explicitly discussed or resolved already (I searched but didn't find any mention)...

The better solution to "fixing" uncovered lines is obviously to (a) structure code to avoid the issue, or (b) write test(s) that cover the line/branch. However, sometimes (at least temporarily), a developer may want to ignore certain lines/branches and explicitly exclude them from the uncovered lines.

I'd propose adding a small bit to `LlvmCovJsonExport::get_uncovered_lines()` after it removes covered lines in a file, it scans the file for lines ending with `//cargo-llvm-cov:ignore`, then uses that to exclude them from being counted in the uncovered lines.

This approach provides a couple advantages:

1. If `--show-missing-lines` is used, it does not show ignored lines (i.e. lines ending with `//cargo-llvm-cov:ignore`), which enables the developer to view and focus on uncovered lines they care about that are not ignored.

2. It flags the lines in source files as being ignored in a way that can be easily found, counted, etc.

I have a functional PoC fork/branch now and a forthcoming PR which will crosslink to this issue.

Additional thoughts/questions:

The first commit in the PR is a humble PoC just to test/prove the approach; it does **not** address any other usability concerns, such as putting this functionality behind an option like `--exclude-ignored-lines`, which would make it opt-in. The second commit will add this. Are there other concerns?

With respect to the project, I'm not aware of any discussion on the topic, etc... please do raise any specific concerns here, either with the topic in general, or with this approach. If this issue/PR can address them, great! Thanks again for an awesome tool!

title: Bug: nextest archive and cargo-llvm-cov do not play well with v2 build-dir layout
body:
Cargo's build-dir layout v2 became the default in nightly recently, which broke [libpathrs](https://github.com/cyphar/libpathrs)'s CI due to an unfortunate combination of behaviours between `cargo-nextest` and `cargo-llvm-cov`. (If you feel this bug report belongs in `cargo-nextest` let me know -- I mainly opened it here because `cargo-llvm-cov` already has special handling for archives and so can probably add workarounds here more easily.)

`cargo-llvm-cov` uses a heuristic added in #483 to find the right object files by looking for a sibling `fingerprint/` directory in `out/...`. Unfortunately, `cargo nextest archive` does not include those directories in its archive and so if you generate an archive with `cargo llvm-cov nextest-archive` it doesn't work with anything that accepts `--archive-file` or if you manually extract it:

```console
$ cargo llvm-cov --version
cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.0
$ cargo nextest --version
cargo-nextest 0.9.143 (60fa45f63 2026-08-04)
release: 0.9.143
commit-hash: 60fa45f638ffc3f35e74afa65737f45fcd32db2a
commit-date: 2026-08-04
host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

$ cargo init --lib repro ; cd repro
$ cargo +nightly llvm-cov nextest-archive --archive-file archive.tar.zst
   Compiling repro v0.1.0 (/home/cyphar/tmp/nextestfun/repro)
    Finished `test` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.07s
   Archiving 1 binary and 1 standard library to archive.tar.zst
    Archived 4 files to archive.tar.zst in 0.05s
$ tar tf archive.tar.zst
target/nextest/binaries-metadata.json
target/nextest/cargo-metadata.json
target/debug/build/repro/<hash>/out/repro-<hash>
target/nextest/libdirs/host/libstd-<hash>.so

# The tests run fine, but the report fails.
$ cargo +nightly llvm-cov nextest --archive-file archive.tar.zst
  Extracting 1 binary to /home/cyphar/tmp/nextestfun/repro/target/llvm-cov-target
   Extracted 4 files to /home/cyphar/tmp/nextestfun/repro/target/llvm-cov-target in 0.03s
────────────
 Nextest run ID e3a45ec7-671d-4e0f-8e2c-020fa32326ee with nextest profile: default
    Starting 1 test across 1 binary
        PASS [   0.005s] repro tests::it_works
────────────
     Summary [   0.005s] 1 test run: 1 passed, 0 skipped
error: failed to collect object files: not found object files (searched directories: /home/cyphar/tmp/nextestfun/repro/target/llvm-cov-target/target/debug); this may occur if show-env subcommand is used incorrectly (see docs or other warnings), or unsupported commands or configs are used
```

However, the information is available in `binaries-metadata.json`, so maybe `cargo-llvm-cov` should extend its parsing of that metadata to also get the binary directory?

```json
{
  ...,
  "rust-binaries": {
    "repro": {
      "binary-id": "repro",
      "binary-name": "repro",
      "package-id": "path+file:///<path>/repro#0.1.0",
      "kind": "lib",
      "binary-path": "/<path>/repro/target/llvm-cov-target/debug/build/repro/7422088c09ffe390/out/repro-7422088c09ffe390",
      "build-platform": "target"
    }
  }
}
```

The alternative would be to ask `cargo-nextest` to include `fingerprint` into their archives even though they don't use them.

### Workaround ###

If you extract the archive (or modify it) and add the `fingerprint` directory then `cargo-llvm-cov` will handle things correctly:

```console
% rm -rf ./target/llvm-cov-target ; mkdir -p ./target/llvm-cov-target
% tar xvf ./archive.tar.zst -C ./target/llvm-cov-target --strip-components=1
target/nextest/binaries-metadata.json
target/nextest/cargo-metadata.json
target/debug/build/repro/7422088c09ffe390/out/repro-7422088c09ffe390
target/nextest/libdirs/host/libstd-c4cc48c1f268d5ea.so
% for dir in ./target/llvm-cov-target/debug/build/*/*/out; do mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")/fingerprint"; done
% cp profile-data/*prof* ./target/llvm-cov-target # Sourced from a previous test run.
% cargo +nightly llvm-cov report
Filename                                         Regions    Missed Regions     Cover   Functions  Missed Functions  Executed       Lines      Missed Lines     Cover    Branches   Missed Branches     Cover
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/home/cyphar/tmp/nextestfun/repro/src/lib.rs           8                 0   100.00%           2                 0   100.00%           7                 0   100.00%           0                 0         -
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOTAL                                                  8                 0   100.00%           2                 0   100.00%           7                 0   100.00%           0                 0         -
```

title: Support distro-provided LLVM tools without environment variables
body:
On Arch Linux, rust, llvm, and cargo-llvm-cov are all available as official distribution packages, but `cargo llvm-cov` still fails unless LLVM_COV and LLVM_PROFDATA are explicitly exported.

For example:

```text
$ cargo llvm-cov
error: failed to find llvm-tools-preview, please install llvm-tools-preview,
or set LLVM_COV and LLVM_PROFDATA environment variables
```

Arch provides:

```text
/usr/bin/llvm-cov
/usr/bin/llvm-profdata
```

Possible approaches could be:

- fall back to llvm-cov / llvm-profdata from PATH when llvm-tools-preview is
  unavailable;
- read LLVM_COV / LLVM_PROFDATA from Cargo [env] configuration;
- keep current behavior if automatic system LLVM discovery is considered unsafe
  due to LLVM/rustc version compatibility.

Would supporting distro-provided LLVM tools automatically be desirable?

title: File summary reports regions missed that the same profdata's JSON export, lcov and function totals all report covered (twice-compiled crate)
body:
## Summary

On a Rust crate that is compiled twice into one coverage report — the `cfg(test)` lib-test object and
the rlib linked into the package's binary — `llvm-cov`'s file summary reports 3 regions missed in a
file whose region-level data, exported from the same profdata by `llvm-cov export -format=json`,
contains **zero regions with execution count 0 under a per-coordinate maximum across all function
records** (142 distinct coordinate regions; the summary counts 147). `-format=lcov` reports zero
uncovered lines from the same profdata. Functions report 100%.

## Reproduction evidence (version pair, invariance)

- rustc 1.97.0 pinned toolchain; cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.6 and 0.8.7 produce the identical numbers (both
  drive the same toolchain `llvm-cov`); reproduced on macOS and on ubuntu CI runners.
- The miss count is invariant under **twelve** source perturbations, including moving the suspected
  code into another file (the 3 stayed with the ORIGINAL file), de-genericizing the one
  `impl Trait`-argument function (removing a per-caller instantiation split), and adding a test that
  drives the last lib-object-uncovered arm.
- Per-object analysis: every region of the file is executed in at least one object; the two function
  records per function (one per compilation) differ in which regions they cover, and the summary's
  count (147) exceeds the distinct coordinate-region count (142) by exactly the number of cross-copy
  duplicates, three of which are read from the copy that did not run.

## Expected

The file summary's region accounting should agree with the export's region data: a region executed in
any function record at the same source coordinates is covered.

## Impact

A `--fail-under-regions 100` gate is unreachable for this crate shape while every actual view of the
data says the file is fully covered.

Reported from a private repository, so file paths are omitted; happy to produce a minimal public reproduction if the shape (a workspace crate compiled both as the cfg(test) lib-test object and as the rlib its own [[bin]] links, with tests driving each object) is not enough to triage. This may belong to llvm-cov itself rather than the wrapper — filing here first since the wrapper drives the toolchain llvm-cov and you are best placed to route it.

title: The default `--ignore-filename-regex` unconditionally filters `examples` even when `--examples` is passed as an argument
body:
According to https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov#basic-usage, there is an `--examples` flag to only run tests in examples. In theory this can be useful to get code coverage information about examples themselves. However, in practice, the `examples` folder is always excluded in the default regex as implemented here: https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov/blob/511e173dcc78a7f274bd7653416c4a2db2099108/src/report.rs#L919.

Could there be a way to adjust the default regex based on the `--examples` flag being passed? Or to add a separate flag to unfilter examples/benches/tests? Otherwise, one has to rebuild the default `--ignore-filename-regex` (without the `examples` part) and disable the default one (via the unstable `--no-default-ignore-filename-regex` flag).

Example workflow where this happened: https://github.com/gendx/gravity-rs/actions/runs/29507855064/job/87653212948

title: Aggregate missing lines when `--show-missing-lines` is selected.

labels.name: C-enhancement
labels.description: Category: A new feature or an improvement for an existing one

body:
## Feature Request: Aggregate consecutive uncovered lines in `--show-missing-lines` output

### Description

When running `cargo llvm-cov` with the `--show-missing-lines` flag, the output lists every uncovered line individually, even when the lines are consecutive.

For example:

```
Uncovered Lines:
/path/to/project/src/file1.rs: 68, 69, 70
/path/to/project/src/file2.rs: 27, 31, 32, 33, 34, 36, 38, 39, 40, 41, 43, 45, 46, 47, 49, 50, 51, 52, 54
```

This can make the output harder to read, especially for files with many uncovered lines.

### Expected Behavior

It would be very helpful if consecutive line numbers were aggregated into ranges.

For example:

```
Uncovered Lines:
/path/to/project/src/file1.rs: 68-70
/path/to/project/src/file2.rs: 27, 31-34, 36, 38-41, 43, 45-47, 49-52, 54
```

### Benefits

- Improves readability of coverage reports
- Makes it easier to quickly identify gaps in coverage
- Reduces noise in large outputs

### Possible Implementation

This could be implemented by grouping consecutive line numbers into ranges before printing.

### Additional Context

Happy to help contribute a PR if this approach is acceptable.
